commitMessage:
Bug 549457 - Autobuild does nothing on org.eclipse.jdt.core.prefs change

If the file .settings/org.eclipse.jdt.core.prefs changes, JDT does not
automatically rebuild the project. E.g. pulling different settings from
git will not result in a re-build; only changing the settings from the
Java compiler preference page will ask the user if they wish to rebuild
the workspace.

After a change in JDT core, a full build is triggered when such changes
are done. The preference page dialog option to not build on applying
Java compiler preference becomes invalid; this change removes this
dialog option.

In case this new behavior causes problems, e.g. in tooling which
re-generates project files without actually changing them, it is
possible to return to the previous behavior with the VM property:

-Dorg.eclipse.jdt.core.disableAutoBuildOnSettingsChange=true

commitMessage:
Bug 549899 - [cleanup & saveaction] Use Autoboxing and Unboxing

- add new AutoboxingCleanUp and UnboxingCleanup classes
- add new usesGivenSignature() static method to ASTNodes class
- add UI support for autoboxing/unboxing to UnnecessaryCodeTabPage
- add new tests to CleanUpTest

Change-Id: Ib859dde76aead8905ab73d53b6e69589b2d2dfb0
Signed-off-by: Fabrice-TIERCELIN <fabrice.tiercelin@yahoo.fr>
dslRule:
<!id: unboxing.primitiveValue>
<!description: Replace explicit calls to Wrapper.primitiveValue() with the wrapper object directly, relying on Java's unboxing feature (Java 5+).>
<!severity: HINT>
<!map UNBOXING_METHODS: "booleanValue" => "java.lang.Boolean",
                        "byteValue" => "java.lang.Byte",
                        "charValue" => "java.lang.Character",
                        "shortValue" => "java.lang.Short",
                        "intValue" => "java.lang.Integer",
                        "longValue" => "java.lang.Long",
                        "floatValue" => "java.lang.Float",
                        "doubleValue" => "java.lang.Double"
>

$x.#{UNBOXING_METHODS_KEY}() :: instanceof($x, "#{UNBOXING_METHODS_VALUE}")
=> $x
;;
summary: Replaces explicit calls to wrapper.primitiveValue() methods (e.g., Integer.intValue()) with the wrapper object directly, relying on Java's automatic unboxing feature introduced in Java 5. The rule ensures that the receiver object is indeed the corresponding wrapper type using an instanceof guard.

Bug 544975 - 'Open Project' does not refresh before opening

With this change OpenProjectAction will trigger a background refresh for
the project, ensuring that the project resources are up-to-date if the
project changed in the file system while being closed. This can e.g.
occur due to an update in the projects repository.

Change-Id: I37826029cc23e075ca7e11cc33a0f762875eb720
Signed-off-by: Simeon Andreev <simeon.danailov.andreev@gmail.com>
dslRule:
<!id: eclipse.core.resources.IProject.open.backgroundRefresh>
<!description: Adds IResource.BACKGROUND_REFRESH flag when opening an IProject with a SubProgressMonitor, ensuring resources are up-to-date.>
<!severity: HINT>
org.eclipse.core.resources.IProject $project.open(new org.eclipse.core.runtime.SubProgressMonitor($monitor, 1))
=>
$project.open(org.eclipse.core.resources.IResource.BACKGROUND_REFRESH, new org.eclipse.core.runtime.SubProgressMonitor($monitor, 1))
;;
